newsitem.title: FRANCE: French anti-racists fight NF in Toulon.
newsitem.headline: French anti-racists fight NF in Toulon.

text.p: Anti-racist militants fought members of the extreme rightist National Front (NF) party during the July 14 Bastille Day parade in this south France naval port on Monday, eyewitnesses said.
Municipal police were also involved in the scuffles, but there was no immediate indication if anyone was hurt or if arrests were made. Toulon's mayor is from the anti-immigration Front.
NF party leader Jean-Marie Le Pen was present on the reviewing stand when the incidents took place, the eyewitnesses said.

The clashes began when Fode Sylla, head of the SOS-Racisme anti-racist group, also invited to the parade's reviewing stand by FN mayor Jean-Marie Le Chevallier, showed up with about 50 members of his movement.
The eyewitnesses said blows were exchanged as the anti-racists chanted "Liberty, Equality, Fraternity" in reply to shouts of "Le Pen president."
Trouble had been expected after Sylla said his group would defy a ban by Le Chevallier to go ahead with a planned Bastille Day festival in the city later in the day.
The African-born Sylla said Le Chevallier had no grounds for banning the long-planned open-air event.
Le Chevallier, who initially cited a threat to public order, told Reuters he had given prior permission for a jazz festival on the same site and "there is no justification for wanting to occupy it".

But Sylla said: "SOS-Racisme and the organising association call on all citizens to meet on the Zenith square from 4 p.m. (1400 GMT), including the jazz group the mayor is talking about, which is cordially invited to join us in song and celebration." The National Front, which advocates sending home three million immigrants and limiting jobs, social services and public housing to native-born French people, has long been at loggerheads with SOS-Racisme.
The movement has brought private prosecutions against its leader Jean-Marie Le Pen for espousing the theory of racial inequality and making ethnic slurs.
Le Pen was recently fined for calling Sylla a "mad, fat ox".
